newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA sees Europe recovery but at slow pace.
newsitem.headline: SCA sees Europe recovery but at slow pace.

text.p: Swedish forestry group SCA said on Wedesday it expected economic growth in Europe to continue to develop positively for the rest of 1997 even if the recovery was slow.

The company reported a 35 percent rise in six-month profit after financial items to 2.25 billion crowns ($280.4 million) including a capital gain of 425 million, against market expectations of 2.01 billion.

SCA said volume growth for the entire group remained strong, amounting to 10 percent midyear. For the first six months SCA posted a four percent rise in sales to 29.33 billion crowns with a six percent sales rise in the second quarter.

"This is attributable to the effect of reduced average prices, which affected invoicing adversely by eight percent, being offset by a strong volume increase of 10 percent and more favourable currency rates of two percent," SCA said in a statement.
SCA said the outlook for the rest of 1997 was mixed.
"The economic growth in Europe is expected to continue to develop positively during the remainder of the year although the rate of recovery is slow," it said.

It said it expected continuing strong demand for hygiene products but raw material costs were expected to rise. Sales of corrugated board were seen benefiting from increased industrial production in Europe.
